shibuya-scramble-crossing: Shibuya's famous pedestrian crossing, where crowds stream across the intersection together. It is a street-level photo stop, with a different perspective from above.
hachiko-statue: A landmark statue beside Shibuya Crossing at the station's Hachiko Exit. This is a quick photo stop rather than a separate, lengthy sightseeing visit.
shibuya-sky: A rooftop observation deck overlooking Shibuya Crossing and the city. Go for the elevated view; sunset entry is especially popular and needs advance planning.
shibuya-center-gai: A neon-lit pedestrian street in Shibuya, lined with arcades and street activity. Walk through for the neighborhood atmosphere and city footage.
shibuya-parco: A shopping mall mixing Japanese fashion with pop culture. Nintendo TOKYO and Pokemon Center Shibuya share the building with restaurants, including Jikasei MENSHO.
hikiniku-to-kome-shibuya: A restaurant serving charcoal-grilled hamburger patties over rice, rather than burgers in buns. The Shibuya branch uses online registration, so plan this meal ahead.
good-wood-terrace: A Jamaican restaurant serving drum-grilled jerk chicken with rice and peas. This is the Kanye-associated spot in the shortlist, not a steakhouse.
recoco-shibuya-record-cafe: A record cafe where every table has its own turntable. Choose records to listen to with a drink, rather than treating it as a regular coffee stop.
uobei-shibuya-dogenzaka: A sushi restaurant where you order on a tablet and dishes arrive along a high-speed delivery lane. A straightforward stop for a quick sushi meal.
jikasei-mensho-shibuya-parco: A ramen restaurant in Shibuya PARCO's basement food floor. Its creamy chicken broth is the main draw, with a signature version topped with A5 wagyu.
kith-tokyo: Kith's streetwear store in Miyashita Park, spread across the first two floors of the north building. Kith Treats is inside the same location.
supreme-shibuya: Supreme's Shibuya streetwear store in Jinnan. It is one of the brand's three Tokyo locations, alongside the Harajuku and Daikanyama shops in this guide.
grandfather-s: A listening bar playing rock, pop and soul records one track at a time. The atmosphere allows conversation while keeping vinyl music at the center.
jbs-jazz-blues-soul: A tiny vinyl listening bar with a large record collection. This is a quiet, music-first room rather than a place for a loud group night.
the-sg-club: Shingo Gokan's cocktail bar with two distinct spaces: casual Guzzle at ground level and Sip, a basement speakeasy. Choose the setting that suits your evening.
nonbei-yokocho: A lantern-lit alley beside the railway tracks, filled with very small bars. Expect tiny seating areas, split into smaller groups, and check cover charges.
c-la-vi-tokyo: A rooftop bar on Tokyu Plaza Shibuya with views toward the crossing. The sky-bar terrace is the relaxed option; the venue also has a club floor.
omotesando-cat-street-harajuku-shibuya-w: A walking route linking Omotesando's architecture, Cat Street's vintage and streetwear shops, and Miyashita Park in Shibuya. It is a neighborhood wander, not one venue.
chermside-sandwich-harajuku: A sandwich shop on Takeshita Street known for a substantial steak sandwich box with fries. The original shop and second location occupy different floors.
harajuku-gyoza-ro: A Harajuku restaurant centered on gyoza, Japanese dumplings. This is a straightforward dumpling meal stop, with cash payment noted in the supplied guide.
afuri-harajuku: A ramen restaurant serving yuzu shio, a citrus-flavored, salt-seasoned broth. Orders use a ticket machine, making it a quick noodle stop in Harajuku.
tonkatsu-maisen-aoyama: A restaurant serving tender tonkatsu, Japanese breaded pork cutlets, in a converted bathhouse. The food and the unusual setting make it more than a quick snack stop.
yoroniku: A splurge Japanese grilled-meat restaurant offering a chef-selected wagyu beef meal, including truffle sukiyaki. This is a reservation-led dinner rather than a casual walk-in stop.
two-rooms-grill-bar: A grill restaurant and terrace bar in Aoyama with skyline views. It suits a relaxed drink or meal with the city as the backdrop.
kindal-harajuku: A designer resale shop on Omotesando, selling secondhand labels such as Comme des Garcons, Yohji Yamamoto and Margiela. Find it above Lawson on the third floor.
ragtag-harajuku: A Japanese designer resale shop on Cat Street. Browse secondhand fashion here as part of the Harajuku shopping walk, rather than expecting a single-brand store.
2nd-street-harajuku: A branch of the secondhand clothing chain with a focus on streetwear and Y2K styles. It is a thrift-shopping stop rather than a designer flagship.
berberjin: A vintage clothing shop focused mainly on American menswear, especially denim and leather. Go here for older clothing rather than new streetwear releases.
supreme-harajuku: Supreme's streetwear shop in Ura-Harajuku, on the second floor in Jingumae. It is a separate branch from the Shibuya and Daikanyama stores.
domicile-tokyo-pleasures-stockist: A Harajuku concept store that stocks PLEASURES alongside its fashion selection. This is the shortlist's PLEASURES shopping lead, not a standalone PLEASURES store.
uniqlo-harajuku-ut: A UNIQLO store with a large UT graphic T-shirt area and UTme! customization. It also carries Uniqlo U tees and everyday clothing basics.
meiji-jingu: A shrine set in forest beside Harajuku Station. It offers a wooded sightseeing stop next to the area's much busier fashion and shopping streets.
recoco-shimokitazawa: A music-focused cafe in Shimokitazawa for spending time with records and a drink. This RECOCO branch is in the ARISTO building basement, separate from Shibuya.
flamingo-shimokitazawa: A vintage clothing shop specializing in American pieces from the 1940s through the 1980s. Flamingo has several shops around the Shimokitazawa area.
new-york-joe-exchange: A thrift shop in a former bathhouse, stocked with clothing traded in by customers. The secondhand selection and converted building are the main draws.
chicago-shimokitazawa: A vintage clothing shop with a broad mix of secondhand pieces and a used-kimono section. It adds variety to a Shimokitazawa thrift-shopping wander.
safari-koenji: A Koenji vintage retailer with several shops in the neighborhood. Safari 1 is the source guide's pick for its rarer pieces within that collection.
whistler-koenji: A vintage shop with a broad selection and a particular emphasis on leather shoes. It is a footwear-focused stop within the Koenji thrift circuit.
koenji-look-street-pal-arcade: Shopping streets and arcades south of Koenji Station, packed with vintage shops. This entry is a whole area to explore, including the smaller side streets.
starbucks-reserve-roastery-tokyo: A four-floor coffee roastery on the Meguro River, designed by Kengo Kuma. The building also houses the upstairs Arriviamo cocktail bar.
meguro-river-walk: A canal-side walk between Nakameguro and Daikanyama, lined with cafes and small boutiques. Treat it as a leisurely route through the neighborhood rather than one attraction.
daikanyama-t-site: A Tsutaya bookstore campus in Daikanyama with books, magazines and music. It is a browsing stop for printed material and design interests, not a fashion mall.
supreme-daikanyama: Supreme's Daikanyama streetwear shop, separate from its Shibuya and Harajuku branches. The supplied guide describes this location as usually the calmest of the three.
pizza-marumo: A wood-fired pizza restaurant in Ebisu, with the Japanese Umami pizza highlighted in the guide. This is a sit-down meal to build an evening around.
ebisu-yokocho: A covered alley of small Japanese eating-and-drinking stalls, known as izakaya. Expect a lively shared setting for food and drinks rather than a quiet restaurant.
bar-martha: A dark listening bar with large speakers and whisky. The emphasis is on the music, with low voices and no photography expected inside.
bar-trench: A small cocktail bar in Ebisu focused on absinthe and botanical drinks. The intimate room makes it a different experience from the nearby busy drinking alleys.
cafe-aaliya: An old-school Japanese cafe, or kissaten, known for French toast cooked on a griddle. Find it in a basement near Shinjuku-sanchome Station.
ramen-afro-beats: A ramen restaurant near Shinjuku-gyoenmae serving creamy chicken paitan broth. It is another chicken-broth option in the guide alongside Ginza Kagari and Jikasei MENSHO.
fuunji: A tsukemen restaurant serving noodles with a separate chicken-and-fish dipping broth. Expect a queue, but the supplied guide notes that it tends to move quickly.
golden-gai: A compact collection of tiny bars in Shinjuku, many with only a handful of seats. Split into small groups and ask about the cover before settling in.
omoide-yokocho: A smoky alley of yakitori places near Shinjuku's west exit, serving grilled chicken skewers. It is a food stop that can precede a Golden Gai bar visit.
bar-benfiddich: A cocktail bar with an apothecary-style approach and farm-to-glass drinks. This is a reservation-focused cocktail experience rather than a casual stop for a quick beer.
new-york-bar-park-hyatt-tokyo: The high-floor Park Hyatt Tokyo bar associated with Lost in Translation. It combines city views with live jazz, making the room part of the experience.
godzilla-head-hotel-gracery: The large Godzilla head above Hotel Gracery in Kabukicho. It is a quick street-photo landmark that can fit into a walk toward Golden Gai.
ginza-kagari-main: A small counter-seat ramen restaurant tucked into a Ginza alley. Its signature draw is creamy tori paitan, a rich chicken-based noodle broth.
uniqlo-ginza-12-floors-uniqlo-tokyo: This entry covers two nearby UNIQLO stores: the Ginza tower with a UT T-shirt floor, and the separate full-range UNIQLO TOKYO flagship at Marronnier Gate.
abercrombie-fitch-ginza: Abercrombie & Fitch's clothing store in Ginza, close to UNIQLO Ginza. It is a familiar-brand apparel stop within the neighborhood's larger shopping circuit.
dover-street-market-ginza: A multi-floor fashion concept store mixing brands such as Comme des Garcons and Stussy with art installations. It shares a building with UNIQLO Ginza.
nihonbashi-philly-eagles-bar: A Philadelphia-themed Eagles sports bar near Tokyo Station that serves cheesesteaks. It is a food-and-drink stop even when there is no game to watch.
tsukiji-outer-market: The public food-market area in Tsukiji, with sushi, seafood and snack stalls. Come here to eat and browse; the wholesale fish auction moved to Toyosu.
tsukiji-yamacho-tamagoyaki: A Tsukiji snack stop selling tamagoyaki, Japanese rolled omelette, on a stick. It is a small bite to add to an outer-market food walk.
sushi-itadori-bekkan: A sushi restaurant in Tsukiji serving nigiri and seafood rice bowls. Choose it for a more substantial seafood meal during an outer-market visit.
kitsuneya: A street-food stand in Tsukiji known for beef horumon-don, an offal stew served over rice. It is a hearty bowl rather than a sushi stop.
toyosu-market-tuna-auction: A chance to observe the fish-market tuna auction at Toyosu. The dedicated observation deck uses a lottery; a separate upper-floor walkway offers another viewing option.
teamlab-planets: An immersive digital-art attraction where parts of the experience involve walking through water. It is an activity to explore physically, rather than a conventional picture gallery.
senso-ji-kaminarimon: A temple sightseeing stop in Asakusa, combining Senso-ji with the Kaminarimon gateway. Pair it with the nearby Nakamise snack street for a neighborhood walk.
nakamise-dori: The snack-shopping street leading toward Senso-ji in Asakusa. Look for treats such as ningyo-yaki cakes and kibi dango dumplings as you walk toward the temple.
hanayaka-kimono-tea-ceremony: A cultural experience combining men's kimono rental, help getting dressed, and a tea ceremony. English support is included in the plan described by the guide.
tokyo-skytree: A tall observation tower near Asakusa, offering another elevated Tokyo viewpoint. This is a skyline-view attraction, so consider whether it adds something beyond Shibuya Sky.
super-potato-akihabara: A retro-video-game shop spread over several floors in Akihabara, with a small arcade upstairs. It combines browsing older games with a little hands-on play.
radio-kaikan: A multi-floor hobby-shopping building in Akihabara with figures, models and trading cards. It contains separate specialist shops, rather than operating as one single store.
mandarake-complex: A multi-floor collectibles store in a black building in Akihabara. Browse manga, vintage toys, figures and cards across its different sections.
hareruya2-akihabara-tower: A specialist Pokemon trading-card store in Akihabara with a dedicated play space. It is a focused card stop rather than a general anime-shopping building.
gigo-akihabara-arcades: Several multi-floor arcade buildings along Akihabara's Chuo-dori. They offer crane machines, rhythm games and purikura photo booths, so this entry covers more than one location.
andaz-tokyo-rooftop-bar: A rooftop terrace bar on the high floors of Andaz Tokyo. The draw is drinks with views toward Tokyo Tower and the bay.
luis-jdm-experience-daikoku-pa-night-tou: A proposed Japanese-car night tour to Daikoku parking area, with Tokyo photo stops. The Luiz/JBDM operator match is unconfirmed, and police closures can change the route.
street-kart-shibuya-annex-mario-kart-sty: A street go-kart tour driving a loop past Shibuya Crossing, Harajuku and Omotesando. These are public-road vehicles, so the operator's driving-document rules matter.
street-kart-akihabara: A street go-kart tour following an Akihabara, Tokyo Station and Ginza loop. It takes place on public roads, not a closed racetrack or arcade simulator.
shinjuku-batting-center: An old-school batting-cage venue in Kabukicho where you hit machine-pitched baseballs. Bats and helmets are provided, making it a straightforward activity stop.
meiji-jingu-gaien-batting-golf-range: A former golf practice range and batting dome, now permanently closed. This record remains only to correct the original shortlist, not as a place to visit.
72tokyo-shibuya-golf-simulator-bar: An indoor TrackMan golf-simulator lounge in Shibuya that also operates as a bar with karaoke. It offers virtual golf rather than an outdoor driving range.
round1-stadium-divercity-tokyo-plaza: An indoor entertainment venue in DiverCity with bowling, arcade games, karaoke and Spo-cha sports activities. The sports selection includes batting, basketball, futsal and go-karts.
alvark-tokyo-b-league-at-toyota-arena-to: Professional basketball games at TOYOTA ARENA TOKYO in Odaiba, with an arena game-day show. This is a dated live sporting event, so choose the correct fixture.
korakuen-hall-boxing-pro-wrestling: A venue for live wrestling and other combat-sports events in Tokyo Dome City. Each organizer sells tickets for its own event, so choose the actual show.
asakusa-sumo-club: A sumo entertainment show featuring retired wrestlers, a chanko meal and a chance to enter the ring. It is a visitor experience, not a professional tournament.
hirakuza-ginza-sumo-live-restaurant: An English-language sumo dinner show in Ginza with a Japanese meal, theatrical lighting and an audience challenge. It combines dining with staged sumo entertainment.
shinjuku-sumo-club: A sumo show hosted in English with retired professionals, photo opportunities and a lottery for audience participation. It is a performance experience, not a tournament.
gold-s-gym-harajuku-tokyo: A Gold's Gym location in Harajuku with a bath and sauna. Visitors need to meet its guest-entry requirements, so it is not an unrestricted drop-in workout.
minami-aoyama-shimizuyu-sento: A neighborhood public bathhouse near Omotesando with soft-water and carbonated baths, plus a sauna and cold plunge. Check its entry restrictions before planning a soak.
tokyo-toyosu-manyo-club-onsen: A hot-spring bathing complex in Toyosu using water brought from Hakone and Yugawara. It includes a rooftop foot bath with views across the bay.
spa-laqua-tokyo-dome: A natural hot-spring spa in Tokyo Dome City, near Korakuen Station. It is a bathing and relaxation stop that can pair with the area's fight venue.
hub-shibuya-british-pub-sports: A branch of the HUB British-style pub chain with screens for football and other sports. It is a casual drinks option in Shibuya's Udagawacho area.
the-bellwood: A wood-paneled cocktail bar in Okushibuya from the SG Group. Come for cocktails and the character of the room, rather than a sports-bar or club setting.
